independence_basis: separate process, fresh session, clean checkout, integrity verified

findings.evidence: finish(): when job is None (create/assign failed) it only calls kill_pid_tree (taskkill /T, which misses a detached grandchild whose parent already exited) and returns contained=False without recording anything; when api.terminate/_wait_empty raises OSError it returns contained=False without appending the job to _OPEN_JOBS (handle also never closed, so KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE never fires). precheck() inspects only _OPEN_JOBS, so the next reviewer's containment_pre is contained=True. run_cmd ignores finish()'s result for gates. Repro with a fake kernel32: /tmp/uri_review_R2/probe_precheck.py prints 'implementer finish: {contained: False, job not created...}' then 'reviewer precheck : {contained: True, killed: 0}' and 'reviewer finish: {contained: True}'; /tmp/uri_review_R2/probe_terminate.py prints 'job 1 active: 1' then 'precheck: {contained: True}'. This contradicts the plan's design ('any containment API failure: contained=False (fail closed)'; 'Before each worker, every earlier job must still show 0') and the doc claim at URI_DEVELOPMENT_LIFECYCLE.md, and reopens the R8-01 threat (an earlier worker's process running alongside the reviewer) on Windows.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a module-level 'tainted' record: any spawn without a job, or any finish() whose terminate/verify raised, makes every later precheck() return contained=False (until the owner unblocks), or keep the failed job in _OPEN_JOBS so precheck re-checks it. Add fake-kernel32 tests for both sequences (uncontained implementer/gate then reviewer precheck; terminate failure then precheck).
findings.title: Windows precheck() is fail-open after an earlier worker/command that had no job or whose TerminateJobObject failed

findings.evidence: init(): when baseline.remote_branch is absent, base = rev-parse baseline.ref; 'expect' is optional. A config written in the old form ('ref': 'origin/integration/git-sync-20261008') reads whichever repository 'origin' is, possibly a stale tracking ref, with no canonical_url comparison. SKILL.md and TEMPLATE.json now use remote_branch, so this matters only for old or hand-written configs.
findings.suggested_fix: For a real milestone require baseline.remote_branch (or refuse a baseline.ref under refs/remotes/ / '<remote>/...') and require 'expect'.
findings.title: baseline.ref still accepts a remote-name tracking ref (e.g. origin/...) without the canonical_url check

findings.evidence: canonical_remote uses 'git remote get-url <name>' (fetch URL). integrate() runs 'git push <remote>', which uses remote.<name>.pushurl / url.*.pushInsteadOf if set. A remote with a canonical fetch URL and a different pushurl present at plan time would push the candidate to another repository. The subsequent ls-remote (fetch URL) then reports PUSH_FAILED, so there is no false INTEGRATED, but the outward push has already happened.
findings.suggested_fix: Also require that 'git remote get-url --push --all <name>' normalises to canonical_url, else BLOCKED REMOTE.
findings.title: canonical_remote compares only the fetch URL; push goes to pushurl/pushInsteadOf
